deviations.what: The pinned simulator daemon (microduck sim-remote-io 0cd676d, robotd 0.10.0) speaks API_VERSION 16 and has NO policy.*, account.*, robot.policies, robot.skills or robot.loadPolicy methods — the policy channel (API 18+, robotctl policy load/add/search/check) landed on main after the sim branch forked. The plan (c6, c8, c33, t17/t18/t19/t21) assumed main's API 23. Proposed resolution: (1) ipc/proto.py is transcribed from the pinned commit as-is (API 16); (2) the policy noun's slot/skill verbs are implemented against main's documented method names and, on a daemon that answers METHOD_NOT_FOUND, exit 2 with a named 'daemon API 16 has no policy channel — needs API >= 18' remediation instead of being silently absent; (3) on the pinned build the skills list is read from robot.subscribe's SubscribeResult (walk/stand/unavailable + per-skill file names) and rules check accepts --skills snapshots; robot.policies is used only when the hello api_version >= 18; (4) the Python fake serves both shapes behind its api_version setting so tests cover both daemons; (5) t23 records the API-16 limits verbatim in the verification doc.
deviations.reason: Discovered by probing the real built daemon before wave 1 merged; the pinned branch is 87 commits behind main and predates the policy channel.

deltas.behavior_text: Policy-channel verbs (policy load/add/remove/reset/list) target upstream main's methods (robot.loadPolicy {slot,path}, robot.setSkill, robot.removeSkill, robot.policies) and on the pinned API-16 daemon exit 2 with a 'needs API >= 18' remediation; the skills list comes from robot.subscribe on API 16; Hub sources print the robotctl line because fetching lives in updaterd

Engine metrics: achieved_hz is the wall-clock cadence (start-to-start) and the work-only figure is published separately as capacity_hz; the first live run showed '5935 Hz achieved' on a paced 50 Hz loop
Intent payloads name the yaw-rate axis vyaw (the wire's and upstream docs' name) instead of wz; the sink no longer renames
Discrete channels (skill, stop, mode) are edge-triggered in the sink: a behaviour holding the channel sends robot.do once, not once per tick; continuous channels are never de-duplicated

The train lane resolves the RL clone the way env doctor does (DUCK_SIM_RL > MICRODUCK_RL_CLONE > ../microduck_rl) and names a missing clone as an environment error; the first smoke attempt leaked 'unexpected: FileNotFoundError'
On-box verification is a recorded manual walkthrough (docs/verification/2026-09-04-sim-bringup.md) plus an optional real-daemon CI job, not the pytest suite against a real socket

The recording contract: duck record writes {ts, source, params} JSONL with a hello head record and raw remoteSessionActive answers; behavior/replay.py reads exactly that shape (reconciled after t17/t18 built the two ends in parallel)

On-box verification is an opt-in pytest suite (tests/live, marker 'live') that operates the CLI end to end against the real daemon on both bodies, run here and by the optional real-daemon CI job; the earlier manual walkthrough (docs/verification/2026-09-04-sim-bringup.md) remains the record of the first run

In the MuJoCo body at the pinned commits, 'duck move' engages the walk policy (policy=walk, twist applied) but the network outputs a static pose, so the duck does not advance; stand-up, skills, rules and every operate verb work on the sim body. Upstream's own drive shape gives the same result and its launcher does not start at this pin pair (body_server lacks --cameras).
